lesson.title: Strings and Text
lesson.driving_question: How can a program clean and present text entered by a user?
lesson.primary_concept_family: String methods return cleaned or formatted copies of text.
misconceptions: String methods return a new string; they do not rewrite the original value.
strip() removes leading and trailing whitespace, not internal spaces.
A variable name must match exactly when it is used.

blocks.definition: A text operation written after a string or variable with a dot. The method name is followed by parentheses.
Returns a copy of a string with spaces removed from the beginning and end. Spaces inside the text remain.
Returns a copy of a string with the first letter of each word changed to a capital letter.
A string method returns new text. Assign the result to a variable if the program needs to use it later.
Ask for text, remove unwanted spaces, change the case and then display the result. One operation on each line makes the program easy to trace.
blocks.example:
name = input("What is your first name? " )
name = name.strip()
name = name.title()
print("Hello,", name)
